overview: Two unconventional infectious agents, one built on nucleic acid replication and the other entirely protein-based.
genZNote: Virus needs genetic instructions. Prion is just a misfolded protein starting a chain reaction.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: An infectious agent composed of nucleic acid and protein that replicates using host cell machinery.
aspects.valueB: An infectious, misfolded form of a normal host protein (PrP) that propagates by inducing normal protein copies to misfold.

aspects.label: Nucleic Acid Content
aspects.valueA: Contains DNA or RNA as its genetic material.
aspects.valueB: Contains no nucleic acid at all — composed purely of misfolded protein.

aspects.label: Mechanism of Propagation
aspects.valueA: Uses its genome (with host machinery) to direct synthesis of new viral components and assemble new virions.
aspects.valueB: Physically templates the misfolding of normal cellular prion protein into the abnormal conformation, without any replication of genetic material.

aspects.label: Classic Examples
aspects.valueB: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, bovine spongiform encephalopathy ("mad cow disease"), kuru.

aspects.label: Resistance to Inactivation
aspects.valueA: Generally inactivated by standard sterilization, disinfection, and often by nucleic acid-damaging treatments.
aspects.valueB: Extraordinarily resistant to standard sterilization methods including autoclaving and most disinfectants, due to a lack of nucleic acid targets.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Purely protein-based infectious agent, no nucleic acid.
